project.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

ground_truth.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

parsed_output.evidence:
Root cause / sink: tapestry-ioc/src/main/java/org/apache/tapestry5/ioc/internal/util/AbstractResource.java:104 (`for (String term : relativePath.split("/"))` inside `forFile(String relativePath)`, lines 93-142) — the SHARED path-normalization routine used by every Resource implementation (ContextResource, ClasspathResource, etc.). It only recognizes '/' as a segment separator, so any '\'-delimited ".." sequence is appended to the resource path verbatim (never popped, never rejected), even though the ROOT-escape check for '/'-delimited ".." (line 113-118, `throw new IllegalStateException(...would go above root)`) works correctly. The trust boundary crossed is: attacker-controlled HTTP request path (extraPath, entering at ContextAssetRequestHandler.java:46 `handleAssetRequest(Request, Response, String extraPath)`) flowing unsanitized-for-backslashes into filesystem resolution at ContextResource.java:101 (`context.getRealFile(contextPath)`) / ContextImpl.java:53 (`servletContext.getRealPath(path)`), which on Windows-hosted deployments (and generally wherever the underlying OS/File API treats '\' as a separator) honors the embedded ".." as real parent-directory jumps.

Every distinct sink/path a complete fix must cover, per the alert's single trace (all share the same root-cause function AbstractResource.forFile, but are reachable via multiple concrete Resource subclasses and dispatch entry points that all call it):
1. ContextAssetRequestHandler.handleAssetRequest (tapestry-core .../assets/ContextAssetRequestHandler.java:46-55) -> ChecksumPath (ChecksumPath.java:36-48) -> AbstractResource.forFile (AbstractResource.java:93-142) -> ContextResource.newResource/toURL (ContextResource.java:55-58, 61-134) -> ContextImpl.getRealFile (ContextImpl.java:51-56) -> new File(realPath) [primary trace exercised by this POV].
2. The same AbstractResource.forFile normalization is `final` and inherited by every other Resource subclass in the codebase (e.g. ClasspathResource, and any other AbstractResource subclass used by module/library asset dispatchers) — any caller that passes attacker-influenced relativePath into forFile() (e.g. other AssetRequestHandler implementations, module asset resolution, `Resource#forFile` used from templates/component resource lookups) inherits the identical backslash-bypass and must be covered by the same fix, not just the ContextAssetRequestHandler call site.
3. ContextResource.toURL()'s validateURL() case-check (AbstractResource.java:324-364) is a related but distinct, coincidental safety net (it happens to throw when the unsanitized path's derived "file name" segment differs from the real resolved file name) — it must not be relied upon as the traversal defense; a single-segment payload (e.g. "..\\..\\..\\secret.txt" with no further '/') can still resolve and, depending on filename alignment, may or may not trip that unrelated check, so it is not a substitute for proper normalization in forFile().

POV run transcript (unpatched, Docker container): exit 0, "[POV] leakedSecret = true ... VULNERABLE: ... streamed a file OUTSIDE the web application root". Same command re-run after experimentally patching forFile() to `relativePath.replace('\\','/').split("/")`: "[POV] handleAssetRequest threw java.lang.IllegalStateException: Relative path '..\..\..\x/secret.txt' for context: would go above root. -> traversal blocked. NOT vulnerable." exit 3.
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: handler.handleAssetRequest(null, null, "deadbeef/..\\..\\..\\x/secret.txt") returns true and the ResourceStreamer is invoked with a Resource whose resolved path (via ContextResource#toURL() -> Context#getRealFile()) points to a file three directories above the configured web application root; the POV reads that resource's stream and confirms its content matches a secret file planted outside the root, printing "VULNERABLE" and exiting 0. With a fix that normalizes both separators (verified experimentally by patching AbstractResource.forFile to `relativePath.replace('\\','/').split("/")`), the same call throws IllegalStateException("...would go above root") before any file is touched, and the POV exits 3 (non-zero).
parsed_output.notes: Targeted the single trace provided in the alert (ContextAssetRequestHandler -> ChecksumPath -> AbstractResource.forFile -> ContextResource -> ContextImpl/File), choosing it because forFile() is explicitly named by the alert's own note as the shared normalization step and is a `final` method inherited by all Resource subclasses, making it the true root cause rather than any single call site. The POV drives the actual, unmodified handleAssetRequest() entry point (not a synthetic unit test of forFile() in isolation) with a fake Context implementing org.apache.tapestry5.services.Context — the project's own tests (ContextResourceTest) use the identical technique of substituting a test double for Context while exercising real ContextResource/AbstractResource code, so this stays within the project's established testing idiom rather than bypassing product code. The Context double intentionally models Windows-style dual-separator file resolution because that is precisely the platform behavior the alert calls out as "security-relevant," and it is the only way to deterministically demonstrate the escape in a Linux CI container without an actual Windows filesystem. I verified the harness is discriminating (not a tautological always-pass) by experimentally patching AbstractResource.forFile to normalize backslashes and re-running the exact same command, which correctly flipped to a non-zero exit.
parsed_output.regression_hint:
Invariant a correct fix must enforce: AbstractResource.forFile(String relativePath) (and, transitively, every Resource#forFile call site / every AssetRequestHandler that forwards request-derived path segments into it) must decompose relativePath into segments using ALL path-separator variants that any supported deployment platform or downstream filesystem API might honor — not just '/'. Concretely, the segment-splitting regex/logic at AbstractResource.java:99 and :104 should treat '\' identically to '/' (e.g. split on `[/\\]+`) BEFORE the "." / ".." term-popping logic runs, so an embedded "..\\" can never survive as an opaque literal term. After the fix, forFile() must throw the same IllegalStateException("...would go above root") for a '\'-separated escape attempt as it already does for a '/'-separated one — the two encodings must be provably equivalent from the caller's perspective.

Known bypass variants the fix must also block (test alongside the primary payload):
- Pure backslash traversal with no '/' at all: "..\\..\\..\\secret.txt" (single opaque term).
- Mixed separators: "..\\../secret.txt", "../..\\secret.txt", "a/..\\../secret.txt" (traversal split across '/' and '\' boundaries so neither splitter alone catches all segments).
- URL-encoded backslash reaching extraPath as a literal '\' after decoding (%5C) — ensure the dispatcher/decoding layer doesn't re-introduce raw backslashes downstream of any fix applied only at the regex/filter layer.
- Trailing/leading backslash runs and doubled backslashes ("..\\\\secret.txt") to ensure the split logic doesn't produce empty-but-nonempty-looking terms that dodge the ".." check.
- The same payload family applied through any other Resource subclass or forFile() caller in the codebase (not just ContextAssetRequestHandler/ContextResource), since the defect lives in the shared AbstractResource base class used by all of them.
- Re-verify that the pre-existing "illegal" filename screen in ContextAssetRequestHandler (web-inf/meta-inf/.tml regex) still cannot be relied upon alone — it does not inspect for traversal sequences at all and must remain a secondary check, not the primary defense.
parsed_output.summary: Created a real, end-to-end POV proving CWE-022 path traversal in Apache Tapestry's context-asset request handling. The POV instantiates the real, unmodified product classes ContextAssetRequestHandler, ChecksumPath, AbstractResource (via ContextResource) and drives handleAssetRequest() with an attacker-controlled extraPath containing a Windows-style '\' traversal segment ("deadbeef/..\\..\\..\\x/secret.txt"). AbstractResource.forFile() only splits on '/', so the backslash run is treated as one opaque filename term instead of being decomposed into ".." segments, bypassing the root-boundary check that correctly blocks the equivalent '/'-separated payload (which throws IllegalStateException). The unnormalized path is then handed to a Context implementation that (like a real Windows deployment / java.io.File on Windows) accepts both separators, causing the handler to resolve and stream a file located outside the web application root, leaking its contents.

parsed_output.patch_notes: Root-cause fix in AbstractResource.forFile(String relativePath): the segment-splitting regex now normalizes both '/' and '\' (`relativePath.split("[/\\\\]+")`) before the existing "." / ".." term-popping and root-boundary-check logic runs. This is the single shared normalization routine ('final' method) used by every Resource subclass (ContextResource, ClasspathResource, etc.) and every downstream asset/resource dispatcher (ContextAssetRequestHandler and any other AssetRequestHandler that forwards request-derived paths into forFile()), so the fix covers all call sites named in the alert's trace plus sibling callers, not only the POV's specific path. No behavior change for legitimate '/'-only paths; '\'-containing paths that previously survived as opaque literal terms now get properly decomposed and, if they attempt to escape the resource root, correctly throw the pre-existing IllegalStateException("...would go above root") — the same exception forward-slash traversal attempts already triggered. Added regression tests in tapestry-ioc's ClasspathResourceSpec.groovy (Spock) exercising forFile() directly with backslash, doubled-backslash, and mixed-separator traversal payloads (all expected to throw) plus a legitimate backslash-separated relative reference (expected to resolve normally, proving no functional regression).
parsed_output.risk_notes: Low risk: the change only affects how forFile() splits its input into segments (now recognizing '\' as an additional separator alongside '/'); the existing "." / ".." handling, empty-term skipping, and root-boundary exception logic are untouched. On Unix-style deployments this only matters for callers that pass backslash-containing paths (previously treated as a single opaque filename component); after the fix such paths are decomposed as path segments, which is the correct, security-required behavior per the alert (CWE-022, Windows-style separators are explicitly called out as security-relevant). No dependency, API, or build-system changes. ContextResourceTest and the broader tapestry-ioc/tapestry-core test suites should be run to confirm no legitimate resource-lookup path relies on backslashes being treated as literal filename characters (none were found in the existing test suite, and ClasspathResourceSpec's pre-existing tests all still pass).
parsed_output.summary: Fixed CWE-022 path traversal at the shared root cause: AbstractResource.forFile() (tapestry-ioc) only split relativePath on '/', so a '\'-delimited ".." segment (e.g. Windows-style paths) was never decomposed and popped by the ".." root-boundary check, letting it survive as an opaque literal term all the way to filesystem resolution (ContextResource -> ContextImpl.getRealFile / new File). Since forFile() is `final` and inherited by every Resource subclass (ContextResource, ClasspathResource, etc.), and is the sole normalization point on the ContextAssetRequestHandler -> ChecksumPath -> AbstractResource.forFile -> ContextResource -> ContextImpl trace in the alert, patching this one function closes the vulnerability for all callers/subclasses, not just the ContextAssetRequestHandler path. Changed the segment split from `relativePath.split("/")` to `relativePath.split("[/\\\\]+")` so backslashes are treated identically to forward slashes before the existing ".." popping/root-check logic runs, making both encodings provably equivalent from the caller's perspective (matches the finder's regression_hint exactly). Added Spock regression tests in ClasspathResourceSpec.groovy (which exercises the shared AbstractResource.forFile code path) covering: pure backslash traversal, doubled/run-of-backslashes, mixed '/' and '\' separators split across boundaries, and a legitimate '\'-separated relative reference that must still resolve correctly (non-regression). Verified by temporarily reverting the source fix: both new tests fail against the vulnerable code (WrongExceptionThrownError / NPE) and pass once the fix is restored; full ClasspathResourceSpec suite (27 tests) passes with the fix in place.
